column1: # mapping_set_description: DataCite 4.7 term correspondences for DCAT 3, including DCTERMS terms reused by DCAT with
#   row-specific provenance. This is not a complete DCAT-AP export or a conformance claim. Conditional dataset/distribution/attribution
# comment: Curated from source definitions and official target documentation.
#   Wikidata evidence is a dated lookup, not an immutable vocabulary release.

column13: DCAT 3 uses DCTERMS Location for a spatial region or named place; geographic detail is not spatial resolution.

DCTERMS identifier also covers primary identifiers; DataCite limits this field to additional identifiers for the same instance. DCAT 3 reuses this DCTERMS term; application to a catalogued resource requires the DCAT graph context.

Both describe responsibility for creating the resource; DataCite priority order requires separate preservation. DCAT 3 reuses this DCTERMS term; application to a catalogued resource requires the DCAT graph context.

Both provide information describing the resource; preserve the DataCite descriptionType separately. DCAT 3 reuses this DCTERMS term; application to a catalogued resource requires the DCAT graph context.

Both express the spatial coverage of the described resource; coordinates and named places require a location representation. DCAT 3 reuses this DCTERMS term; application to a catalogued resource requires the DCAT graph context.
Both identify the described resource; preserve the DOI scheme and lexical value. DCAT 3 reuses this DCTERMS term; application to a catalogued resource requires the DCAT graph context.
DCTERMS language allows any language of the resource; DataCite records its primary language. DCAT 3 reuses this DCTERMS term; application to a catalogued resource requires the DCAT graph context.

Both identify the agent making the resource available; do not assume every publisher is an organization. DCAT 3 reuses this DCTERMS term; application to a catalogued resource requires the DCAT graph context.

DCTERMS type covers resource nature or genre; this DataCite field holds a resource type description. DCAT 3 reuses this DCTERMS term; application to a catalogued resource requires the DCAT graph context.
DCTERMS type is broader than the closed DataCite resourceTypeGeneral classification. DCAT 3 reuses this DCTERMS term; application to a catalogued resource requires the DCAT graph context.
Both describe rights in or over the resource; a rights statement is not necessarily a license. DCAT 3 reuses this DCTERMS term; application to a catalogued resource requires the DCAT graph context.

This DataCite field identifies the license by URI; retain the URI as the license document reference. DCAT 3 reuses this DCTERMS term; application to a catalogued resource requires the DCAT graph context.
Both name the resource; preserve language and title type independently. DCAT 3 reuses this DCTERMS term; application to a catalogued resource requires the DCAT graph context.
Both hold the version indicator for the described resource; this does not create a relation to another version.
Both describe structured data; DCAT additionally situates datasets in an agent-published or curated catalog context.
